standard_prerequisites.name: For a short exact sequence of complexes the determinant of the middle differential corresponds to the tensor product of the determinants of the outer differentials, functorially
standard_prerequisites.use: Decomposes det(d_K) as det(d_M) tensor det(d_L).

core_obligations: Write M^i = Ker(a^i); the hypotheses on a give a map of short exact sequences 0 -> M^{-1} -> K^{-1} -> L^{-1} -> 0 over 0 -> M^0 -> K^0 -> L^0 -> 0 with connecting differentials d_M, d_K, d_L (proof lines 36993-37007). By the det-ses-functorial lemma the determinant det(d_K) corresponds to det(d_M) tensor det(d_L) as maps (proof lines 37008-37010). Since L has rank 0 its determinant line contributes trivially, and unwinding the determinant identifications of the ses lemma against the definitions of the canonical elements delta(K) and delta(L) gives det(a)(delta(K)) = delta(L) (proof lines 37010-37012).
proof_roadmap: Factor through the kernels to get the map of short exact sequences (proof lines 36993-37007).
Apply the determinant multiplicativity of the ses lemma and unwind to the canonical elements (proof lines 37008-37012).
